results:
The results cover the de Bruijn criterion in general but say nothing about Automath or who coined the term, so the Automath link is unconfirmed here.

- **Core idea:** A proof assistant meets the criterion when a small, independent checker can verify its output, so the complex search machinery doesn't need to be trusted. One survey describes this as a proof kernel that filters all the mathematics, and notes that HOL Light's kernel is only several hundred lines of OCaml. The survey attributes the criterion to the idea that correctness should be guaranteed by a small checker, meaning the system has a proof kernel that filters all the mathematics.
- **Design practice:** The Rocq documentation says that separating the kernel from the elaboration engine and tactics follows this principle, so users can rely on complex external plugins because the kernel checks their output. (Rocq docs, index 7-1 to 7-3)
- **Open problem:** A 2025 paper notes that certifying the kernel itself has been achieved for higher-order logic (HOL Light via Candle) but is still missing for dependent type theory. An equivalent achievement for dependent type theory is still missing, despite 30 years of efforts since Barras.

I did not find a source confirming de Bruijn's role in Automath, so a follow-up search on "Automath de Bruijn history" would be needed to verify that part.

Here's what the search turned up on Automath and de Bruijn's background.

**Automath:** Wikipedia describes it as a formal language that de Bruijn began devising in 1967 for expressing complete mathematical theories, with a built-in proof checker to verify them. It was also reportedly the first practical system to exploit the Curry–Howard correspondence, and de Bruijn arrived at that correspondence independently of Howard's work. Many of its ideas, such as dependent types, were later adopted or reinvented in typed lambda calculus and related areas.

**Origins:** A memorial volume notes that de Bruijn was already an established mathematician when, at 49, he chose in 1967 to move into automating mathematics. Per the same source, his interest came from the newly emerging computer technology, which led him to start a project to check mathematical texts with computer help. The system was written in Algol 60 and ran on the limited computers of the 1960s.

**De Bruijn's background:** He was born in The Hague in 1918 and died in Nuenen in February 2012. He was a Dutch mathematician who worked in analysis, number theory, combinatorics and logic. He earned his doctorate in 1943 at the Free University of Amsterdam under Jurjen Koksma, with a thesis on algebraic number theory. Much of his early learning was self-directed because of wartime conditions, a habit of independence that the sources say shaped his later work.

**Further reading:** Rob Nederpelt and Francien Dechesne wrote an article on the path from de Bruijn's mathematical practice to Automath in *The Mathematical Intelligencer* (vol. 34, issue 4). The Eindhoven University of Technology site hosts background material on the project, including a reprinted 1991 article on checking mathematics with computer assistance.

content.text:
**答案：尼古拉斯·戈弗特·德布鲁因（Nicolaas Govert de Bruijn，1918–2012）。**

他从 1967 年起设计 Automath，这是一种用来形式化数学理论、并带有内置证明检查器的语言。“de Bruijn 准则”说的是：证明助手的输出应由一个小而独立的检查器（内核）来验证，所以复杂的搜索和策略部分不必被信任。

第一次搜索的结果只讲了这条准则本身，没有直接说它以德布鲁因命名。准则的名字和 Automath 的作者都是德布鲁因，这一点是我根据常识和两次搜索的结果合起来得出的结论，没有哪个来源明确写出这一整句话。

Sources:
- [Nicolaas Govert de Bruijn – MacTutor](https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/De_Bruijn/)
- [Automath – Wikipedia](https://www.Wikipedia.org/wiki/Automath)
- [About Automath – TU Eindhoven](https://www.win.tue.nl/automath/aboutautomath.htm)
- [A Survey on Theorem Provers in Formal Methods](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.03028)
- [Rocq 文档：核心语言](https://rocq-prover.org/doc/v9.3/refman/language/core/index.html)
